mainTopic: The cities walled since יהושע, whether the first קדושה of ארץ ישראל lasted forever, and counting יובל in עזרא's time
overview: The גמרא explains a ברייתא that names גמלא, גדוד, חדיד, אונו and ירושלים as cities walled since the days of יהושע בן נון. אביי reads the names as boundary points, and רבא reads the regions as labels that tell us which city of a shared name is meant. The גמרא asks how ירושלים can be on the list, since a house there never becomes חלוט. רבי יוחנן answers that the list means cities like ירושלים, and רב אשי answers that there were two places called ירושלים. Next, two ברייתות of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי seem to disagree about whether the first קדושה of the land lasted forever. The גמרא answers that two תנאים reported his view differently, or that the 'forever' view really belongs to רבי אלעזר בר יוסי. It then brings the sources for each side: the פסוק about the סוכות in עזרא's time, and the פסוק 'which your fathers inherited.' Finally it asks how יובל could be counted in עזרא's time, and רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that they counted it only to keep the שמיטה years in the right place.

steps.title: אביי explains the list as a set of boundary points
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the ברייתא as giving boundary markers in each region: up to גמלא in the גליל, up to גדוד in עבר הירדן, and חדיד, אונו and ירושלים in יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what the ברייתא means. Up to גמלא in the גליל, up to גדוד in עבר הירדן, and חדיד, אונו and ירושלים in יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains what the ברייתא's list of place names is really saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads the ברייתא as marking out regions. In the גליל the walled cities reach up to גמלא, and in עבר הירדן they reach up to גדוד. In יהודה it names three specific walled cities: חדיד, אונו and ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means: a way of rereading a text to explain it
Up to, until; here it marks a boundary point
The land on the eastern side of the Jordan river

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא that lists these cities, which the גמרא was just discussing.

phrases.english: Up to Gamla in the Galilee,
up to Gedod in Transjordan,
and Ḥadid and Ono and Jerusalem in Judea.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי הכי קאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a ברייתא discussed just before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא gives boundary points for walled cities in each region
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Walled cities run up to גמלא in the גליל and up to גדוד in עבר הירדן, and in יהודה they include חדיד, אונו and ירושלים

steps.title: רבא says the regions just tell us which city of that name is meant
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the regions are there to identify which גמלא and which גדוד the משנה means, because other cities share those names. The other cities in the משנה have unique names, so they need no region.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: "גמלא in the גליל" excludes a גמלא in other lands. "גדוד in עבר הירדן" excludes a גדוד in other lands. The other cities have no namesakes, so the ברייתא did not need to name a region for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different reading of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the regions are not boundaries. They are labels that tell us which city the משנה means. Cities with unique names, like יודפת, need no label, which is why the ברייתא does not mention them.

keyTerms.meaning: Other lands, meaning the other regions
Like them, meaning another city with the same name

phrases.english: Rava said: Gamla in the Galilee,
to exclude a Gamla of other lands;
Gedod in Transjordan,
to exclude a Gedod of other lands;
those others, where there are none like them,
phrases.notes: He means the other cities listed in the משנה, which no other town shares a name with.

phrases.english: it was not necessary for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבא אמר גמלא בגליל לאפוקי גמלא דשאר ארצות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same ברייתא that אביי explained
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the ברייתא adds region names
steps.terutzMaskana: The regions identify which city of a shared name is meant

steps.title: But a house in ירושלים never becomes permanently sold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ירושלים can be listed as a walled city where a sold house becomes the buyer's forever, since a ברייתא says a house in ירושלים never becomes חלוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a house in ירושלים become permanently the buyer's? But a ברייתא teaches: ten things were said about ירושלים, and one is that a house there does not become permanently the buyer's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that ירושלים belongs on this list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a city walled from the days of יהושע, a sold house that is not redeemed within a year becomes the buyer's forever. Another ברייתא says ירושלים is special and this never happens there. So how can ירושלים be listed among these cities?

keyTerms.meaning: Permanently sold, owned by the buyer forever
Ten things: ten special laws about ירושלים

phrases.english: And in Jerusalem, does it become permanent?
phrases.notes: "It" is a house that was sold and not bought back within a year.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Ten things were said about Jerusalem,
a house does not become permanently sold in it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וירושלים מי מיחלט בה והתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inclusion of ירושלים in the list both readings accepted
steps.kashyaTarget: Listing ירושלים as a walled city where houses become חלוט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says a house in ירושלים never becomes חלוט, so it cannot follow the walled-city rule

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the list means cities like ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the list means cities that are like ירושלים in being walled since יהושע, not ירושלים itself. In those cities a sold house does become חלוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It means cities like ירושלים, which are walled since the days of יהושע בן נון, but not exactly like ירושלים. In ירושלים a house never becomes permanent, while here, in those cities, a house does become permanent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge by rereading "ירושלים" in the list as "like ירושלים."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The listed cities share one feature with ירושלים: they were walled since the days of יהושע. They do not share ירושלים's special law. So the house-selling rule applies in them but not in ירושלים itself, and the two sources no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: From the days of יהושע בן נון, when the land was first conquered

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying ירושלים lacks a wall from יהושע's time. He is saying ירושלים has its own special exception, while the other walled cities follow the normal rule.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Like Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמוּקֶּפֶת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן,
phrases.english: which is surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua son of Nun,
but not like Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם אֵין הַבַּיִת חָלוּט בָּהּ,
phrases.english: for whereas in Jerusalem a house does not become permanently sold,
here a house does become permanently sold in it.
phrases.notes: Some versions say בהן (in them) in the round brackets; the square brackets give the corrected wording, בָּהּ (in it). Either way the meaning is the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יוחנן כירושלים דמוקפת חומה מימות יהושע בן נון
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the ten things said about ירושלים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text to mean a comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ירושלים itself was listed as a city where a house becomes חלוט
steps.terutzMaskana: The list means cities walled like ירושלים, and in them a house becomes חלוט, unlike in ירושלים itself

steps.title: רב אשי: there were two places called ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer. Just as רב יוסף said there were two places called קדש, there were also two places called ירושלים. The list means the other one, where houses do become חלוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Didn't רב יוסף say there were two places called קדש? Here too, there were two places called ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second way to answer the challenge about ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי keeps the word "ירושלים" as a real city name. He says it is a different town with the same name, so the special law of the holy city does not apply to it. He borrows the idea from רב יוסף, who solved a different problem by saying there were two places called קדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't...? Opens a question that expects a yes
Here too, applying the same idea

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why ירושלים is on the list of walled cities. רבי יוחנן says it means cities like ירושלים. רב אשי says it is a second city named ירושלים. Either way, in the holy city of ירושלים a sold house never becomes חלוט.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לָאו אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Didn't Rav Yosef say
there were two places called Kadesh?
Here too, there were two places called Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב אשי אמר לאו אמר רב יוסף תרי קדש הוו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the קשיא, different from רבי יוחנן's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a different place with the same name
steps.terutzMaskana: The ירושלים in the list is a second town with that name, where houses become חלוט

steps.title: Why only these cities were listed: the first holiness ended
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי says the חכמים listed these cities because the returning exiles found them and sanctified them. The original walled cities lost their status when the land's קדושה ended. The גמרא concludes that he holds the first קדושה was only for its time.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי says: Why did the חכמים list these cities? Because when the exiles came back, they found these and sanctified them. The first ones lost their status when the holiness of the land ended. So he holds that the first holiness was only for its own time, not for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא explaining why the משנה lists only these particular walled cities. It then draws out what this חכם must hold about the first קדושה of the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original walled cities from יהושע's time lost their status at the exile. Only cities that were sanctified again by the returning exiles count. The גמרא sums this up with the word קסבר: the first קדושה was temporary.

keyTerms.meaning: The exiles who came back from בבל in the time of עזרא
The first sanctification of the land, in the days of יהושע
He holds; the גמרא's way of saying what a חכם's view implies

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether the first קדושה of the land lasts forever is a major question. It affects which places count as holy for many מצוות.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei says:
Why did the Sages count these cities?
Because when the exiles came up
they found these and sanctified them,
but the first ones lost their status
when the holiness of the land ended.
He holds: the first holiness sanctified for its time,
and did not sanctify for the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי למה מנו חכמים את אלו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the list of cities in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only cities re-sanctified by the returning exiles count. The first קדושה was only for its time.

steps.title: A second ברייתא of the same Sage seems to say otherwise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a contradiction. It brings another ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי. This one points out that there were many more walled cities, like the sixty cities of ארגוב. So why were only these listed?
steps.simpleTranslation: They raise a contradiction. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said: Were these the only walled cities? The פסוק already says, 'sixty cities, all the region of Argob... all these were fortified cities.' So why did the חכמים list these? Because when the exiles came back, they found these and sanctified them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a second ברייתא from the same חכם in order to show a contradiction. The real clash only shows up at the end of this ברייתא, in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening of this ברייתא sounds like the first one. The problem comes later, when it says the first קדושה lasts forever. So this step is the setup for that clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction; this introduces a source that seems to clash
The region of Argob, east of the ירדן

phrases.english: And they raise a contradiction:
Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said:
Were these the only ones?
But hasn't it already been said:
"Sixty cities, all the region of Argob...
all these were fortified cities"!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָמָּה מָנוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת אֵלּוּ?
phrases.english: So why did the Sages count these?
Because when the exiles came up
they found these and sanctified them.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורמינהי אמר רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי וכי אלו בלבד היו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא of the same חכם to contradict step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view in step 6 that the first קדושה was only for its time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same חכם seems to hold, in another ברייתא, that the first קדושה lasts forever. This becomes explicit in step 10.

steps.title: Did they really need to sanctify them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops in the middle of the ברייתא. The phrase 'they sanctified them' can't be right, because later in this same ברייתא it says no sanctifying was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They sanctified them'? But we say that they didn't need to sanctify them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא interrupts the quote to point out that one phrase in the ברייתא doesn't fit the rest of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of this ברייתא says the first קדושה lasts forever. If so, the cities were still holy, and there would be nothing to sanctify. So the word 'sanctified' can't be meant literally here.

keyTerms.meaning: We say; here it points to a later line in the same ברייתא

phrases.english: They sanctified them?
But we say that there is no need to sanctify them!
phrases.notes: This points ahead to the end of this same ברייתא (step 10), which says the first holiness lasts forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: קידשום הא אמרינן דלא צריך לקדושינהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions one word in the ברייתא quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word וקידשום in the second ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sanctifying would be pointless if the first קדושה never ended, and that is what this ברייתא says later.

steps.title: Read it as 'they counted them'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the word: it should be 'they counted them', not 'they sanctified them'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read: they counted them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects the wording of the ברייתא so it fits the ברייתא's own ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exiles did not make these cities holy. They only identified them and listed them. That is why these cities appear in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: They counted them, or listed them

phrases.english: Rather, they counted them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא מנאום
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by changing the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exiles actually sanctified the cities.
steps.terutzMaskana: They only listed the cities. The cities were already holy.

steps.title: The second ברייתא says the first holiness lasts forever
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא continues: any city with a family tradition that it was walled since יהושע keeps all these מצוות, because the first קדושה lasts forever. This is the direct contradiction to step 6.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only these cities. Any city where you have a tradition from your ancestors that it was walled since the days of יהושע בן נון keeps all these מצוות. This is because the first holiness sanctified for its time and also for the future!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the second ברייתא. Now the contradiction is out in the open: here the same חכם says the first קדושה is forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said the first קדושה ended. Here he says it never ended. The same חכם seems to hold two opposite views.

keyTerms.meaning: Since the days of יהושע בן נון

steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות say 'the exiles found these.' The real difference is only in the last line: one says the first holiness was for its time only, the other says it was also for the future.

phrases.english: And not only these,
but any city for which you have a tradition
in your hand from your ancestors

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמּוּקֶּפֶת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן —
phrases.english: that it was walled since the days of Joshua son of Nun —
all these מצוות apply in it,
because the first holiness sanctified for its time
and sanctified for the future!

steps.triggerLanguage: ולא אלו בלבד אלא כל שתעלה לך מסורת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that began in step 7, after the wording fix in steps 8–9.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 6, where רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי holds that the first קדושה was only for its time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same חכם says the opposite here: the first קדושה lasts forever.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about what רבי ישמעאל held
steps.stepSummary: First answer: two תנאים reported רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's opinion differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: these are two תנאים, and they disagree about what רבי ישמעאל held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות come from different reporters, who each passed down רבי ישמעאל's view differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל himself did not contradict himself. Two later תנאים disagree about which view he held.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; introduces one possible answer
According to, about the opinion of

phrases.english: If you want, say: two Tannaim
disagree about the view of Rabbi Yishmael,

steps.triggerLanguage: איבעית אימא תרי תנאי ואליבא דרבי ישמעאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different תנאים reporting one חכם's view differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי held two opposite views.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two תנאים disagree about what his view was.

steps.title: The second ברייתא was really said by רבי אלעזר בר יוסי
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: one of the ברייתות, the one saying the first קדושה lasts forever, was actually said by רבי אלעזר בר יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: one of them was said by רבי אלעזר בר יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer: the second ברייתא has the wrong name on it. Its real author is רבי אלעזר בר יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this answer, רבי ישמעאל consistently holds that the first קדושה ended. The 'forever' view belongs to his brother, רבי אלעזר בר יוסי.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: one of them
was said by Rabbi Elazar bar Yosei,

steps.triggerLanguage: ואיבעית אימא חד מינייהו רבי אלעזר בר יוסי אמרה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same contradiction answered in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות are from רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'forever' ברייתא is from רבי אלעזר בר יוסי.

steps.title: Proof: רבי אלעזר בר יוסי holds the old wall still counts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר בר יוסי reads 'אשר לוא חומה' to mean a city counts as walled even if it has no wall now, as long as it had one before. That fits the view that the first קדושה lasts forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר בר יוסי says, 'which has [לוא] a wall' teaches that even if it has no wall now, if it had one before, it counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its second answer by showing that רבי אלעזר בר יוסי holds a view that matches the second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לוא is spelled with an alef, so it can be read as 'no'. The verse then hints at a city that has no wall now but once had one. If the old status stays even without the wall, that matches the idea that the first קדושה lasts forever.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Which has a wall'; the word לוא is spelled with an alef, so it can be read as 'no wall'

steps.whatToRemember: Step 6 says the first קדושה was for its time only. Step 10 says it lasts forever. The גמרא answers either that two תנאים disagree about רבי ישמעאל's view, or that the 'forever' view really belongs to רבי אלעזר בר יוסי.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Elazar bar Yosei says:
"Which has a wall" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:30. Since לוא is spelled with an alef, it can also be read as 'which has no wall'.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עַכְשָׁיו
phrases.english: even though it does not have one now
but it had one before.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתניא רבי אלעזר בר יוסי אומר אשר לוא חומה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר בר יוסי holds the old walled status stays, like the view that the first קדושה lasts forever.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His reading of 'אשר לוא חומה' in a ברייתא.

steps.title: What is the source for 'the first sanctity was only for its time'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the view that the first קדושה did not last forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who says the first sanctity of the land was only for its own time, and not for the future?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks where the view that the first קדושה ended comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10-13 showed there are two opinions about whether the first קדושה lasts forever. Now the גמרא wants the source for the view that it was only temporary.

keyTerms.meaning: The first sanctity of the land, from when יהושע brought the people in

phrases.english: What is the reason of the one who says:
the first sanctity sanctified for its time
and did not sanctify for the future to come?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling who holds which view, the גמרא now asks for the source of the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for the view that the first קדושה was only temporary.

steps.title: The פסוק about the סוכות in עזרא's time
steps.stepSummary: The source is a פסוק in נחמיה saying the returning exiles made סוכות as had not been done since יהושע's days.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'The people of the exile who came back from captivity made סוכות and sat in them, for since the days of יהושע בן נון the Jewish people had not done so, and there was very great joy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from נחמיה as the starting point of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say that nobody had made סוכות between יהושע and עזרא. The גמרא will soon show that this cannot be literal, and that hidden meaning becomes the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The people who came back from the Babylonian exile

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the people of the exile who returned from the captivity made
sukkos, and they sat in the sukkos,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא עָשׂוּ מִימֵי יֵשׁוּעַ בִּן נוּן
phrases.english: for they had not done, since the days of Yeshua son of Nun,
phrases.notes: נחמיה 8:17. ישוע here is just another spelling of יהושע.

phrases.english: so, the children of Israel, etc.
and there was very great joy."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the first קדושה ended

steps.title: The פסוק cannot be read literally
steps.stepSummary: Could it be that even in דוד's time nobody made סוכות until עזרא came? Surely not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it possible that דוד came, and still nobody made סוכות until עזרא came?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the plain meaning of the פסוק cannot be true. So the פסוק must mean something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under kings like דוד the Jewish people surely kept סוכות. So 'not done since יהושע' cannot mean nobody made סוכות. The question pushes us toward a deeper reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible?, used for a question that expects the answer 'no'

phrases.english: Is it possible that David came

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עָשׂוּ סוּכּוֹת עַד שֶׁבָּא עֶזְרָא?
phrases.english: and they did not make sukkos until Ezra came?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶפְשָׁר בָּא דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal reading of the פסוק quoted in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal meaning of the פסוק in נחמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is impossible that סוכות went unkept through דוד's reign and all the generations after, so the פסוק must mean something else.

steps.title: עזרא's return is compared to יהושע's entry
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק compares the two entries into the land: both times they counted שמיטה and יובל and sanctified walled cities anew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק compares their coming in עזרא's days to their coming in יהושע's days. Just as in יהושע's days they counted שמיטה and יובל years and sanctified walled cities, so too in עזרא's days they counted שמיטה and יובל years and sanctified walled cities.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real meaning of the פסוק. It is a comparison between עזרא's return and יהושע's entry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they had to sanctify the land all over again in עזרא's time, the first קדושה must have stopped at the exile. That is exactly the view of step 14: the first קדושה was only for its time.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, linking two things so one teaches about the other
Entry, the coming into ארץ ישראל

steps.whyThisMatters: This היקש is the core source for the view that the land's קדושה from יהושע's time ended at the exile and had to be renewed.

phrases.english: Rather, it compares their coming in the days of Ezra
to their coming in the days of Yehoshua:
just as at their coming in the days of Yehoshua
they counted Shemitah and Yovel years
and sanctified walled cities,
so too at their coming in the days of Ezra
they counted Shemitah and Yovel years
and sanctified walled cities.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַקִּישׁ בִּיאָתָם בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty of step 16 by reading the פסוק as a comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the פסוק as a היקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק literally says nobody made סוכות from יהושע until עזרא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק compares the two entries: both required counting the years and sanctifying walled cities anew, so the first קדושה had ended.

steps.title: A second פסוק: your inheritance is like your fathers'
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in דברים compares the later inheritance of the land to the fathers' inheritance, so all these מצוות had to be renewed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק also says: 'ה׳ your God will bring you to the land that your fathers inherited, and you will inherit it.' It compares your inheritance to your fathers' inheritance. Just as your fathers' inheritance came with starting all these things fresh, so too your inheritance comes with starting all these things fresh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second פסוק to support the same view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the word 'inherit' twice ties the return from exile to the first conquest. Since the first conquest started everything new, so does the return. That means the earlier קדושה did not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: And it also says, bringing a second פסוק as more support
Inheritance, taking possession of the land

steps.whatToRemember: The view that the first קדושה was only temporary rests on two היקשים: נחמיה's comparison to יהושע, and דברים's comparison of 'your inheritance' to 'your fathers' inheritance'.

phrases.english: And it says:
"And ה׳ your God will bring you to the land
that your fathers inherited, and you will inherit it."
It compares your inheritance to the inheritance of your fathers:
just as the inheritance of your fathers
was with the renewal of all these things,
phrases.notes: 'All these things' means the מצוות tied to the land's holiness, like שמיטה, יובל and walled cities.

phrases.english: so too your inheritance
is with the renewal of all these things.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second scriptural support to the היקש of step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the first קדושה ended and had to be renewed

steps.title: How does the other view read the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the view that the first קדושה lasts forever explains the פסוק in נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, how does he explain the פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks how the other side deals with the פסוק in נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view that the first קדושה lasts forever cannot accept the comparison of step 17. It still has to explain why the פסוק says nothing like this had been done since יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning how the opposing view handles this

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This is the view that the first קדושה lasts forever, the one connected to רבי אלעזר בר יוסי in step 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the temporary-קדושה view to the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the view that the first קדושה lasts forever explains the strange wording of the פסוק in נחמיה.

steps.title: The 'סוכה' was protection from a prayer against עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: They prayed to remove the desire for עבודה זרה and succeeded, and that merit sheltered them like a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They prayed for mercy about the desire for עבודה זרה and cancelled it, and that merit protected them like a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other view's reading. The 'סוכה' in the פסוק is a picture of protection, not a real booth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the thing not done since יהושע was the removal of the desire for עבודה זרה. The פסוק says nothing about renewing the land's קדושה, so the first קדושה can still last forever.

keyTerms.meaning: The drive or desire to worship idols

steps.whatToRemember: Both views must explain 'not done since יהושע'. One view reads it as a renewed קדושה of the land. The other reads it as the merit of cancelling the desire for עבודה זרה, which sheltered them like a סוכה.
steps.confusionAlert: On this view, the 'סוכה' is not a real booth. The פסוק is using it as a picture of the protection that the merit gave them.

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְעוֹ רַחֲמֵי עַל יֵצֶר דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: That they prayed for mercy regarding the desire for idol worship,
and they cancelled it,
and the merit protected them like a sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְעוֹ רַחֲמֵי עַל יֵצֶר דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק refers to a protective merit, gained by cancelling the desire for עבודה זרה, that sheltered them like a סוכה. It does not refer to renewing the land's קדושה.

steps.title: The פסוק hints at criticism of יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in נחמיה spells יהושע's name as ישוע, hinting that he is being criticized.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is why the פסוק is strict with יהושע: everywhere else his name is written 'יהושע', but here it is written 'ישוע'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a note to the story from step 20. The פסוק in נחמיה shows displeasure with יהושע by spelling his name differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the people in עזרא's time prayed and removed the desire for עבודה זרה. The פסוק compares them to the days of יהושע. Writing his name in a shorter form signals that he could have done this and did not.

phrases.english: And this is why the verse is strict
with Joshua,
for in every place it is written "Yehoshua,"
and here it is written "Yeshua."
phrases.notes: נחמיה 8:17. Here his name is spelled in a shorter form.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּקָא קָפֵיד קְרָא עִילָּוֵיהּ דִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the explanation of the נחמיה פסוק from step 20 by pointing to the unusual spelling of יהושע's name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spelling 'ישוע' in נחמיה shows that the פסוק criticizes יהושע.

steps.title: Why יהושע, and not משה, is criticized
steps.stepSummary: משה had no merit of ארץ ישראל to pray with, but יהושע did, so he should have prayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that משה did not pray for mercy, because he did not have the merit of ארץ ישראל. But יהושע did have that merit, so why didn't he pray?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the criticism falls on יהושע and not on משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'why didn't he pray' is not a real challenge to the גמרא. It explains the criticism. משה never entered the land, so he lacked its merit. יהושע brought the people into the land, so he had the merit needed for such a prayer to work.
steps.confusionAlert: This 'why didn't he pray' is not the גמרא attacking an earlier statement. It is the reason behind the criticism of יהושע.

phrases.english: Granted, Moses did not pray for mercy,
since there was no merit of Eretz Yisrael,
but Joshua,
who had the merit of Eretz Yisrael,
why didn't he pray for mercy?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מֹשֶׁה לָא בְּעָא רַחֲמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the criticism of יהושע hinted at in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע had the merit of ארץ ישראל and should have prayed. משה lacked it, so he is not blamed.
steps.whatToRemember: This closes the side story. The people in עזרא's time succeeded where יהושע did not even try, and the פסוק hints at this with his shortened name.

steps.title: A challenge from the verse about the fathers' inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'which your fathers inherited and you shall inherit it' seems to require taking possession of the land again, against the view that the first קדושה lasts forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'Which your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the view from step 19, that the first קדושה never ended, and challenges it with the פסוק quoted in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 this פסוק was used to show that the later return to the land matched the first entry, with everything done anew. If the land had to be inherited anew, its holiness seems to have stopped. That contradicts the view that the first קדושה lasts forever.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it written (introduces a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"Which your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it"!
phrases.notes: דברים 30:5. This is the same פסוק used back in step 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כְתִיב: אֲשֶׁר יָרְשׁוּ אֲבוֹתֶיךָ וִירִשְׁתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side story to the argument over whether the first קדושה ended.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the first קדושה of the land lasts forever.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק seems to compare the later inheritance to the first one, so the land had to be made holy again.

steps.title: Your fathers' inheritance is already yours
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means that because your fathers inherited the land, you already inherit it. Nothing needs to be renewed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: since your fathers inherited it, you have inherited it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the פסוק in a new way that fits the view that the first קדושה lasts forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge read the פסוק as 'you must inherit it again, just like your fathers did.' The answer reads it as 'your fathers' taking of the land already counts for you.' So the original holiness simply carries over.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
since your fathers inherited it,
you have inherited it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּיָרְשׁוּ אֲבוֹתֶיךָ יָרַשְׁתָּ אַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק requires a fresh inheritance, so the land needed new holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fathers' inheritance carries over automatically, so the first קדושה never ended.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views can read the same פסוק. One sees a fresh start. The other sees the fathers' holiness continuing.

steps.title: Could they really count יובל in עזרא's time?
steps.stepSummary: יובל stopped once some tribes were exiled. In עזרא's time only about 42,000 people returned, so how could they count יובל?
steps.simpleTranslation: But did they really count שמיטה and יובל years then? Now, once the tribes of ראובן and גד and half the tribe of מנשה went into exile, יובל stopped. So in עזרא's time, when the whole community was only 42,360, would they have counted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from step 17, which said they counted שמיטה and יובל when they returned with עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is a קל וחומר. Even when most of the Jewish people still lived in the land, the exile of two and a half tribes stopped יובל. In עזרא's time only a small group came back. Surely יובל could not be counted then.

keyTerms.meaning: now, if... (opens a 'how much more so' argument)

phrases.english: But did they count שמיטה and יובל years?
Now, if from when the tribe of Reuven was exiled
and the tribe of Gad and half the tribe of Menashe
the יובל years stopped,
then Ezra, about whom it is written
"The whole congregation together

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע רִבּוֹא אַלְפַּיִם וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשִׁשִּׁים״
phrases.english: was forty-two thousand, three hundred and sixty"
phrases.notes: עזרא 2:64. A רבוא is ten thousand, so literally it says four רבוא, two thousand, six hundred and sixty.

phrases.english: would he have counted?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָנוּ שְׁמִיטִּין וְיוֹבְלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the claim in step 17 that they counted שמיטה and יובל in עזרא's time.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that they counted שמיטה and יובל when they returned with עזרא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if a partial exile canceled יובל while most of the people were in the land, then a tiny returning group certainly could not keep it.

steps.title: Proof that יובל needs all the inhabitants in the land
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that יובל stopped when ראובן, גד and half of מנשה were exiled, because the פסוק requires all the land's inhabitants to be living on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: once the tribes of ראובן and גד and half of מנשה were exiled, יובל stopped. The פסוק says, 'And you shall proclaim freedom in the land to all its inhabitants.' This means only when all its inhabitants are living on it, and not when some of them have been exiled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the starting point of its challenge, that יובל stopped once part of the people went into exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'all' in the פסוק is read as a condition. יובל applies only when the whole people lives in the land. This strengthens the question from step 25 about עזרא's small community.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that יובל applies only when all of the Jewish people are living in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
From when the tribe of Reuven and the tribe of Gad were exiled
and half the tribe of Menashe,
the יובל years stopped,
as it says:
"And you shall proclaim freedom in the land to all its inhabitants,"
meaning, when all its inhabitants are living on it,
and not when some of them have been exiled.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מִשֶּׁגָּלוּ שֵׁבֶט רְאוּבֵן וְשֵׁבֶט גָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim used in step 25's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That יובל stopped once ראובן, גד and half of מנשה were exiled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 25:10, 'to all its inhabitants', as a requirement that the whole people be in the land.

steps.title: Even mixed-up tribes cancel יובל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that יובל does not apply even when all Jews live in the land, if the tribes are mixed into each other's portions. It learns this from the words 'to all its inhabitants.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that if everyone lives in the land but the tribes are mixed up (בנימין living in יהודה's area and יהודה in בנימין's), יובל still applies. So the פסוק says 'to all its inhabitants': only when the inhabitants live in their proper places, not when they are mixed up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא from the last step. Now it adds a second, stricter condition for יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 said יובל needs all the Jews to be in the land. This clause adds that each tribe must also be in its own portion. In עזרא's time only a small group returned and the tribes were not in their places, so the question of how they counted יובל gets much stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might have thought.' It opens a wrong idea that the ברייתא is about to reject.
'The פסוק teaches.' It brings a פסוק to reject the wrong idea.
Mixed up, intermingled. Here it means tribes living in each other's portions.
In their proper arrangement, with each tribe in its own portion.
The fiftieth year, when land goes back to its original owners and slaves go free.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is still the same ברייתא, adding a stricter condition that makes the question from step 25 harder.

phrases.english: One might have thought: if they were all on it, but they are intermingled,
phrases.notes: 'On it' means living in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: the tribe of Benjamin living in Judah's portion
and the tribe of Judah living in Benjamin's portion,
then the Jubilee should be in effect?
The verse teaches: "To all its inhabitants"
meaning, when its inhabitants are living in their proper arrangement,
and not when they are intermingled!

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל הָיוּ עָלֶיהָ וְהֵן מְעוֹרָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 26 with a second, stricter clause that strengthens the question from step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That יובל could not have been in effect in עזרא's time.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of 'לְכׇל יֹשְׁבֶיהָ': each tribe must live in its proper portion.

steps.title: They counted יובל only to set the שמיטה years
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that in עזרא's time they counted the יובל year only to keep the שמיטה cycle in the right place, not to keep the laws of יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: They counted the יובל years in order to set the שמיטה years correctly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: how could they count יובל when it did not apply? It says the counting was only to fix the dates of the שמיטה years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that counting יובל meant keeping its laws. רב נחמן בר יצחק separates the two. They counted the fiftieth year as יובל so that the next seven-year cycle would start at the right time, but the laws of יובל were not in effect.

keyTerms.meaning: To sanctify, here meaning to set the correct year as holy.
שמיטה years, the seventh years when the land rests.

steps.whatToRemember: In עזרא's time, יובל was counted only to keep the שמיטה calendar correct. Its own laws did not apply, because the land's inhabitants were not all there and in their proper places.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the יובל count can matter for the calendar even when the laws of יובל are not in effect.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
They counted Jubilee years
in order to sanctify the Sabbatical years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 25, which was made stronger by the ברייתא in steps 26-27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the action: counting is separated from keeping the laws.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Counting יובל in עזרא's time meant the laws of יובל were in effect, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: They counted יובל only to set the שמיטה years correctly. The laws of יובל themselves did not apply.
